School should start later, and honestly I don't get why this is still a debate. Teenagers' body clocks shift during puberty, so asking a sixteen year old to be alert at 7:30 is a bit like asking an adult to do algebra at 4 a.m. My first period last year was chemistry. I can tell you almost nothing about chemistry.

People who disagree usually bring up buses and sports. Fair enough, the bus schedule is a real problem, since districts reuse the same buses for elementary and high school routes. But that's a logistics problem, not a reason. Some districts flipped the order so little kids go first, and little kids are awake at six anyway, ask any parent.

The sports argument annoys me more. Practice would end later, sure. But we're saying an extra hour of sleep for two thousand students matters less than daylight for the forty on the soccer team? I play soccer. I'd take the sleep.

I'm not claiming a later bell fixes everything. Kids will still stay up on their phones, me included. But when the schedule fights biology, biology wins, and right now it's winning during first period.
